**How it works:** the two languages treat comments differently, so each compiler hides the other language's code.

1. **Line 1, `// \`:** in C++, a backslash at the end of a line joins it to the next line. That pulls the whole Rust line into the C++ comment. Rust has no such rule, so it treats line 1 as a comment and compiles line 2 (`fn main ...`).
2. **`/* /* */`:** in Rust, block comments nest. This line opens two comments and closes one, so Rust is still inside a comment and skips all the C++ code. In C++, comments don't nest, so the first `*/` ends the comment and the compiler reads the C++ code that follows.
3. **Last line, `// */`:** inside a Rust block comment, `//` has no special meaning, so the `*/` closes the remaining comment. In C++, the whole line is an ordinary `//` comment.

Both versions use 128-bit unsigned integers, so results are exact up to N = 184. For larger N, Rust wraps around on purpose and C++ wraps around naturally, so they still print the same (wrong) value.
